newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit instability unjustified, says central bank.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit instability unjustified, says central bank.

text.p: Malaysia's economic fundamentals do not justify volatility in the ringgit, a central bank official said on Thursday.
"The fundamentals (of the economy) don't warrant instability (in the ringgit)," Zeti Akhtar Aziz, assistant governor of Bank Negara Malaysia said.
She said Bank Negara, the central bank, would continue to defend the ringgit.
"We have a responsibility to ensure stability," she said when asked about Bank Negara's policies on intervention to defend the ringgit.

Bank Negara Governor Ahmad Mohamed Don on Thursday warned of stern measures, including raising interest rates, if speculators continued to attack the ringgit. He also hinted at possible capital controls.
On Tuesday, Bank Negara spent an estimated $1.0 billion to defend the ringgit in the open market.
At 0525 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.4982/87 to a dollar.
